deliverables: Ongoing maintenance including bug fixes, dependency upkeep, security patches, and releases
Dijkstra developer preview with initial Plutus V4 support in the compiler and standard library
Dijkstra ledger rules and transaction-builder updates including new builtins, cost models, nested transactions, accounts, and guard scripts with conformance testing
Improved JS/TS interfaces and documentation for Scalus components embedded in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, and Lucid Evolution
Java/Kotlin integration including Spring Boot and Ktor examples and cleaner integration paths with Cardano Client Lib and Yaci
Application runtime foundational components, reactive workers, chain follower, and task scheduler
request.what: Fund a 9-month continuation of Scalus covering maintenance, Dijkstra hard-fork readiness, interoperability across JVM and JS/TS ecosystems, and a scoped application runtime.

claims.claim: Scalus is an established open-source Cardano development platform built by Lantr Engineering over three years of continuous delivery.
Scalus components are reused in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, Lucid Evolution, Cardano Client Lib, and YaciDevKit.
Protocols and applications including Gummiworm L2, Bifrost, SugarRush, Vela, and DID/DIDComm are built on Scalus.
The proposal states Scalus has 4,642 commits across 32 releases, 12 contributors, and Scalus.js reaches more than 20,000 downloads per month.
The requested budget is ₳2,464,844 for 9 months, equivalent to about $394,375 at a $0.16/ADA reference rate, with no contingency.
This resubmission reduces the previous proposal from ₳8,503,000 over 12 months to about ₳2,464,844 over 9 months and reduces FTE from 8.25 to 2.25.
The proposal excludes a standalone production-grade JVM L1 node, full Gummiworm L2 integration, broad formal verification, and advanced devnet expansion.
Delivery is described as milestone-based through audited SundaeSwap treasury contracts with an independent oversight board and third-party assurance.
Lantr Engineering says every prior milestone was delivered on time and commits to public reporting, open community sessions, and on-time milestone delivery for treasury-funded work.
The proposal frames Scalus as shared open-source infrastructure under the Apache 2.0 license that can reduce repeated assembly work across Cardano teams.

summary: The document requests ₳2,464,844 for Lantr Engineering to continue Scalus for 9 months, focused on maintenance, Dijkstra readiness, interoperability, and a scoped runtime, with several adoption and delivery-record claims stated by the proposer and some metrics presented as externally checkable.
